dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:2201.text: The upper and lower eyelids. From 目; 僉 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2202.text: To move the eyes. From 目; 乏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2203.text: Deep-set eyes; also a surname. From 目; 圭 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2204.text: The pupil or brightness of the eye. From 目; 灷 supplies the sound. Note: 勝 and 賸 both take their sound from 朕; perhaps anciently 朕 was used for 眹.

shuowen:2205.text: The eye's pupil. From 目; 牟 supplies the sound. The Shuowen simply writes 牟.

shuowen:2206.text: The edge of the eye. From 目 and 厓.

shuowen:2207.text: To look left and right. From two 目. All graphs in this category contain 䀠. Pronounced like 拘; also like 瞿瞿 in “the worthy man looks alertly.”

shuowen:2208.text: The enclosure of the eyes. From 䀠 and 纾. Pronounced like 卷 in 書卷. Ancient writing uses it for 醜. [The precise sense of 目圍 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2209.text: Eyes looking sideways. From 䀠 and 大; 大 is a person.

shuowen:2210.text: Hair above the eyes. From 目, depicting an eyebrow; the upper part depicts the forehead's texture. All graphs in this category contain 眉.

shuowen:2211.text: To inspect. From abbreviated 眉 and 屮.

shuowen:2212.text: A shield, 瞂, used to protect the body and cover the eyes. A pictograph. All graphs in this category contain 盾.

shuowen:2213.text: A shield. From 盾; 犮 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2214.text: The grip of a shield. From 盾; 圭 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2215.text: The nose. It depicts a nose. All graphs in this category contain 自.

shuowen:2216.text: A palace or chamber not seen. The explanation is missing. [The recorded gloss 宮不見 is difficult.]

shuowen:2217.text: This too is 自, abbreviated: the breath of speech emerges from the nose and assists the mouth. All graphs in this category contain 𪞶.

shuowen:2218.text: A word meaning all together. From 比 and 𪞶.

shuowen:2219.text: A word meaning dull. From 白; abbreviated 鮺 supplies the sound. The Analects says: “Shen is dull.”

shuowen:2220.text: A particle distinguishing matters. From 𪞶; 纺 supplies the sound. 纺 is the ancient form of 旅. [The unusual recorded component is preserved.]

shuowen:2221.text: A particle. From 𪞶; 𢏚 supplies the sound. 𢏚 is the same as 疇. The Book of Yu says: “The emperor said: 𤾊咨.” [Tentatively: “Who, ah, who？”]

shuowen:2222.text: A particle of recognition. From 𪞶, 亏 and 知.

shuowen:2223.text: Ten tens. From 一 and 𪞶. In counting, ten hundreds make one string, displaying one another. [The final explanatory clause is uncertain.]

shuowen:2224.text: To draw breath through 𢌿. From 自 and 𢌿. All graphs in this category contain 鼻. [The use of 𢌿 in the gloss is unexplained.]

shuowen:2225.text: To approach an odor with the nose. From 鼻 and 臭; 臭 also supplies the sound. Pronounced like 畜 in 畜牲.

shuowen:2226.text: Breathing while lying asleep. From 鼻; 干 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 汗.

shuowen:2227.text: A cold illness blocking the nose. From 鼻; 九 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2228.text: Breathing while lying asleep. From 鼻; 隶 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 虺.

shuowen:2229.text: Two hundred. All graphs in this category contain 皕. Pronounced like 祕.

shuowen:2230.text: Abundant. From 大 and 皕; 皕 also supplies the sound. This was the name of Duke Shao of Yan. Pronounced like 郝. The Scribe's Primer calls it 醜.

shuowen:2231.text: To fly repeatedly. From 羽 and 白. All graphs in this category contain 習.

shuowen:2232.text: Familiarity leading to weariness. From 習; 元 supplies the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Wasting years and idling away days.”

shuowen:2233.text: A bird's long feathers. A pictograph. All graphs in this category contain 羽.

shuowen:2234.text: A bird with strong feathers and a fierce disposition. From 羽; 是 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2235.text: The red-feathered heavenly fowl. From 羽; 倝 supplies the sound. The Lost Book of Zhou says: “The great 翰 resembles a colorful pheasant, also called 鷐風. In King Cheng of Zhou's time the people of Shu presented it.”

shuowen:2236.text: A mountain pheasant with a long tail. From 羽 and 隹.

shuowen:2237.text: A red-feathered bird from Yulin. From 羽; 非 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2238.text: A blue-green-feathered bird from Yulin. From 羽; 卒 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2239.text: Feathers growing. Another explanation: 𠂕羽, apparently shedding or cutting feathers. From 羽; 前 supplies the sound. [The rare gloss is uncertain.]

shuowen:2240.text: Neck feathers. From 羽; 公 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2241.text: A wing. From 羽; 支 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2242.text: A wing. From 羽; 革 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2243.text: Long tail feathers. From 羽; 堯 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2244.text: The base of a feather. Another explanation: the appearance of feathers first growing. From 羽; 矦 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2245.text: The shaft of a feather. From 羽; 鬲 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2246.text: A curved feather. From 羽; 句 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2247.text: Feathers fanning the wind; also an ancient feudal lord. Another explanation: an archery master. From 羽; 幵 supplies the sound. [The opening action is uncertain.]

shuowen:2248.text: To rise in flight. From 羽; 者 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2249.text: To rise. From 羽; 合 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2250.text: To fly a little. From 羽; 瞏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2251.text: To fly broadly. From 羽; 軍 supplies the sound. Another explanation: south of the Yi and Luo, a pheasant displaying all five colors is called 翬. The Odes says: “Like a pheasant taking flight.”

shuowen:2252.text: To fly high. From 羽 and 㐱.

shuowen:2253.text: To fly swiftly. From 羽; 扁 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2254.text: Nimble: rapid flight. From 羽; 夾 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 瀒. Another explanation: to flank or assist, 俠.

shuowen:2255.text: The appearance of flight. From 羽; 立 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2256.text: The appearance of vigorous flight. From 羽 and 冃.

shuowen:2257.text: The appearance of vigorous flight. From 羽; 之 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2258.text: To soar, 翱翔. From 羽; 皐 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2259.text: To fly in circles. From 羽; 羊 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2260.text: The sound of flight. From 羽; 歲 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “The phoenix flies, its feathers rustling.”

shuowen:2261.text: A bird's white, plump, glossy appearance. From 羽; 高 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “White birds, plump and shining.”

shuowen:2262.text: A musical dance: feathers are bound to cover the head in sacrifice to the stars. From 羽; 王 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 皇. [The source's 纣 is unusual.]

shuowen:2263.text: A musical dance holding complete feathers to sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain. From 羽; 犮 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 紱.

shuowen:2264.text: A feather screen used in dancing. From 羽; 𣪐 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “Holding a feather screen in the left hand.”

shuowen:2265.text: An ornate canopy. From 羽; 殹 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2266.text: Feather ornaments hanging down from a coffin: eight for the Son of Heaven, six for lords, four for grandees, two for scholars. From 羽; 妾 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2267.text: To fly. From 羽; 番 supplies the sound. Alternatively from 飛.

shuowen:2268.text: A feather. From 羽; 令 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2269.text: The sound of flight. From 羽; 工 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2270.text: A general name for short-tailed birds. A pictograph. All graphs in this category contain 隹.

shuowen:2271.text: The Chu crow, also called 鸒 and 卑居; Qin calls it 雅. From 隹; 牙 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2272.text: One bird. From 又 holding 隹. Holding one 隹 is 隻; two 隹 is 雙.

shuowen:2273.text: The bird 鵋䳢. From 隹; 各 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2274.text: The bird 今閵, resembling a myna but yellow. From 隹; abbreviated 𨳏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2275.text: The 周燕 bird. From 隹; 屮 depicts its crest, and 㕯 supplies the sound. Another account: King Wangdi of Shu had intercourse with his minister's wife; ashamed, he fled and became the 子巂 bird. Thus when Shu people hear its call they all rise and say “Wangdi.”

shuowen:2276.text: A bird. From 隹; 方 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 方.

shuowen:2277.text: A small bird that lives near people. From 小 and 隹. Pronounced the same as 爵.

shuowen:2278.text: A bird. From 隹; 犬 supplies the sound. Suiyang has the Ya River.

shuowen:2279.text: The bird 雗鷽. From 隹; 倝 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2280.text: There are fourteen kinds: 盧諸雉, 喬雉, 鳪雉, 鷩雉, 秩秩海雉, 翟山雉, 翰雉 and 卓雉; south of the Yi and Luo, 翬; south of the Yangtze and Huai, 搖; in the south, 𢏚; east, 钕; north, 稀; west, 蹲. From 隹; 矢 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2281.text: Male and female calling. When thunder first stirs, pheasants call and extend their necks. From 隹 and 句; 句 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2282.text: A domestic creature that knows the time. From 隹; 奚 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2283.text: A chick. From 隹; 芻 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2284.text: A large young bird. From 隹; 翏 supplies the sound. Another explanation: a pheasant's late-hatched young are called 雡.

shuowen:2285.text: The yellow 倉庚 bird. When it calls, silkworms hatch. From 隹; 离 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2286.text: The bird 鷻. From 隹; 周 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2287.text: A bird. From 隹; abbreviated 瘖 supplies the sound. Alternatively from 人, which also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2288.text: The bird 𨿠. From 隹; 氐 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2289.text: The bird 𨾦. From 隹; 垂 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2290.text: A stone bird, also called 雝𪆫. Another name is 精𠛱. From 隹; 幵 supplies the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Qin had Shi Jian.”

shuowen:2291.text: The bird 雝𪆫. From 隹; 邕 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2292.text: A bird. From 隹; 今 supplies the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary has Prince Ku Qian.

shuowen:2293.text: A bird. From 隹 and 人; 厂 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 鴈.

shuowen:2294.text: 𩁟黃. From 隹; 黎 supplies the sound. Another explanation: the Chu bird, its color dark black and yellow.

shuowen:2295.text: A bird. From 隹; 虍 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2296.text: The bird 牟母. From 隹; 奴 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2297.text: The nine 雇 birds mark farming and silkworm seasons, guarding the people against excess. From 隹; 戶 supplies the sound. Spring 雇 is 鳻盾; summer, 竊玄; autumn, 竊藍; winter, 竊黃; thorn 雇, 竊丹; traveling 雇, 唶唶; night 雇, 嘖嘖; mulberry 雇, 竊脂; old 雇, 鷃.

shuowen:2298.text: A kind of 䨄. From 隹; 𦎫 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2299.text: A kind of 𩁛. From 隹; 酓 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2300.text: A bird. From 隹; 支 supplies the sound. Another explanation: 䧴度, a bird name.
